The core insight is that consciousness enables forward-looking behavior, which is functionally equivalent to predictive modeling. This leads to a dualism between deterministic (vegetative) and probabilistic (conscious) adaptation mechanisms. In GSI, this manifests as Bayesian inference over latent variables where prior beliefs are updated based on new evidence. In GSE, it translates into dynamic state-space models where agents anticipate future states and adjust policies accordingly. The failure mode occurs when predictive models are outdated or when environmental dynamics exceed model capacity. Risk and uncertainty are formalized as the variance in outcome distributions under incomplete knowledge. The economic implications suggest that profit emerges from superior anticipation and adaptation strategies, aligning with the principle of rational expectation in macroeconomic theory.
